c.tagline: Roman ruins, a singing sea, and the world's most beautiful sunset.

taxi.fareNote: Licensed taxis are metered; Uber and Bolt both operate in Zadar and are usually cheaper and easier than hailing on the street.

emergency.note: 112 is the EU-wide emergency number reaching police, fire, and ambulance.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in Old Town summer crowds and around late-night bars in peak season.

hood_desc: The compact peninsula that holds Roman ruins, medieval churches, and the modern Sea Organ and Sun Salutation art installations; everything from the Roman Forum to St. Donatus and the sunset promenade is walkable. Best for first-timers who want sights on the doorstep.

The neighborhood immediately southeast of the peninsula wrapped around the city's main pebble beach; you can swim and still stroll into the old town in minutes, so it's the ideal beach-plus-sightseeing base without a car.
A pine-shaded resort strip about 3.5 km northwest of the center with a long sand-and-pebble beach, a marina, and large family hotels; quieter, greener, and easy for parking.
A laid-back residential seaside area northwest of the center with small coves, family-run rooms, and a genuinely local feel; suits travelers who want calm and a non-touristy pace.
A seaside residential peninsula near Kolovare and Borik lined with beaches, a marina, and unpretentious konoba dining; relaxed and popular with returning summer regulars.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout the city.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 5:00 AM to around midnight; there is no dedicated night network, so taxis or Uber/Bolt fill late-night gaps.
transit.note: Zadar has no metro or tram; getting around means walking the compact old town, riding Liburnija city buses, and taking Jadrolinija ferries and catamarans out to the islands.
transit.pay: A single bus ticket is about €1.59 (valid 50 minutes) bought from the driver or a kiosk; island ferries are ticketed separately at the port.

bus: Intercity coaches from Zadar Bus Terminal (FlixBus, Arriva, Croatia Bus) to Split, Zagreb, Rijeka, and Dubrovnik
ferry: Jadrolinija ferries and catamarans to Ugljan, Dugi Otok, Molat and other islands
Seasonal international ferry Zadar-Ancona (Italy) via Jadrolinija/SNAV
train: Limited regional rail from Zadar station (Croatian Railways) toward Knin and Zagreb - slow, so coaches are usually faster

transit.m: Liburnija airport shuttle to Zadar bus terminal / old town (~20-25 min, timed to flights)
Taxi to the old town (15-20 min)

tip.r: Rounding up the bill or leaving around 10% for good service is appreciated but not expected.

landmarks: Sea Organ (Morske Orgulje)
Marble steps hide underwater pipes that turn Adriatic waves into haunting music—the world's first sea-played instrument, mesmerizing at sunset.
Greeting to the Sun
A 22-meter solar-powered light disc beside the Sea Organ, pulsing with hypnotic color displays after Zadar's famously spectacular sunsets.
Church of St. Donatus
A massive 9th-century Byzantine rotunda built on Roman forum rubble, Zadar's enduring symbol and a superb summer concert venue.
Roman Forum
The largest Roman forum on the Croatian Adriatic, founded under Augustus, littered with columns including the medieval 'Pillar of Shame.'
Cathedral of St. Anastasia
Dalmatia's largest cathedral, a Romanesque beauty whose free-standing bell tower rewards climbers with red-roof and island panoramas.
Riva Promenade
Zadar's seafront walk facing Ugljan island, where Alfred Hitchcock famously declared the sunset the most beautiful in the world.
Five Wells Square
A charming square built over a Renaissance cistern with five ornamental wellheads, wedged between a medieval tower and leafy park.
Land Gate
The Venetian master gate of 1543, crowned by St. Chrysogonus on horseback beneath the winged Lion of St. Mark.
Museum of Ancient Glass
An astonishing collection of delicate Roman glassware salvaged from local tombs, with daily glassblowing demonstrations in a 19th-century palace.
Gold and Silver of Zadar
Benedictine nuns guard this treasury of reliquaries and medieval goldsmithery in St. Mary's convent—one of Croatia's cultural crown jewels.

train.note: Regional trains link Zadar with Knin and onward toward Zagreb, but they are slow and infrequent; almost everyone travels by coach instead.

bus.note: Zadar's bus terminal is the main travel hub, with frequent daily coaches (FlixBus, Arriva, Croatia Bus) to Split (~3h), Zagreb (~3.5h), Rijeka, and Dubrovnik, plus seasonal international lines toward Italy, Slovenia, and Germany.

ferry.note: Jadrolinija and SNAV run seasonal ferries to Ancona, Italy; year-round Jadrolinija ferries and catamarans serve the Zadar archipelago (Ugljan, Dugi Otok, Molat) from the old-town harbor and Gazenica port.
